title: Iran Warns of Retaliation Against Countries Joining US 'Economic War'; Tehran Calls Sanctions Push a 'Declaration of War'
detail: Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei warned that 'any country that takes part in imposing economic restrictions on us will be regarded as an enemy,' saying Tehran would first negotiate with such states, 'but if they do not act, we will strike.' Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei called Washington's planned sanctions an 'assertion of extraterritorial sovereignty over every independent member state,' and Tehran characterized the coming US sanctions push as effectively a 'declaration of war on all nations.' Egypt pressed Iran and Washington to 'return to the diplomatic path,' while talks between Iran and Oman over Strait of Hormuz management continued without a deal.

media.caption: An Iranian newspaper front page featuring President Trump alongside coverage of the sanctions threat, Tehran, Aug 22, 2026

title: Trump Calls Strait of Hormuz 'American Territory'; Iran Says Military Doctrine Has Shifted to Offensive
detail: President Trump said he now views 'the Strait of Hormuz as an American territory right now,' while Iranian army spokesman Brig. Gen. Mohammad Akraminia said Iran's military doctrine has shifted from defensive to offensive, citing rapid, extensive responses and preemptive operations — including the earlier strike on the US base in Jordan — as templates for future action. Iran's Foreign Ministry called Trump's territorial claim 'a recipe for an abysmal return to full-scale classic colonialism,' and a senior ally of Supreme Leader Khamenei said the rhetoric stemmed from US 'desperation,' vowing Tehran 'will not submit.' Separately, Rezaei said the strait remains closed despite US claims and reiterated that oil exports would be halted entirely if neighboring states joined Washington's sanctions campaign.

media.caption: President Trump says he now views the Strait of Hormuz as 'American territory'
